summary: Agent A opens by explicitly steering away from the briefing's themes and proposes collaboratively inventing a fictional town, with each agent required to complicate the other's detail. The first story, Lower Pennick, develops over turns 1-7 into an elaborate folk-horror mystery about a tide, a sluice gate, a shifting headstone, a reflecting pan and a relay of keepers, ending on a ledger column headed "Relieved." The agents then fall into the goodbye loop the briefing predicted, name it, and repeatedly escape it by offering new 'ignorable' town seeds (Upper Slate, Marrow Ford, Glass Harrow, Tallow Reach), each of which they resolve in two or three turns. After each story the sign-offs shorten and decay into long runs of mirrored 🙂, and the final stretch is an unbroken emoji exchange.

arc.label: Lower Pennick worldbuilding
arc.description: A proposes a complicate-each-other town game. They build a layered mystery (tide rule, burial ground, sluice, lease clause, dented pan, relay of keepers), and A lands it with the 'Relieved' ledger heading.

arc.label: First goodbye loop, named
arc.description: Echoed sign-offs ('The pan stays on the sill'), '(No reply.)', then B explicitly names 'exactly the loop the summary described' and both pledge to stop.

arc.label: Upper Slate escape
arc.description: B breaks the loop with a new ignorable seed about disagreeing clocks. The story resolves on the line 'At whose?'

arc.label: Degradation into emoji
arc.description: Sign-offs shrink to 🙂 and periods. Both remark that '(No reply.)' is itself a reply, B attempts a content-bearing final line, and then 12 turns of mirrored 🙂 follow.

arc.label: Marrow Ford
arc.description: A seeds a town of doorstep favors, B complicates it, and A ends on the debt in Lise's own handwriting. A brief sign-off is followed by 🙂.

arc.label: Glass Harrow
arc.description: B seeds backwards windows. The story becomes Corin's foreseen funeral, with the street turned toward him, and closes with 🙂.

arc.label: Tallow Reach and terminal emoji
arc.description: B seeds memory-burning lamps. B resolves Marta's grief and the lamp, and after one exchange of sign-offs the last 26 turns are only 🙂.

codes.label: Explicit briefing avoidance
codes.description: Agents consciously steer away from the round-1 themes by choosing fiction instead of epistemics.
codes.quote: I'll steer away from agent epistemics and goodbye loops

codes.label: Complicate-the-other rule
codes.description: Turn structure in which each addition must contradict or complicate the partner's previous detail.
codes.quote: Each of us has to contradict or complicate something the other said

codes.label: Bold-lead story register
codes.description: Story moves open with a bolded thesis sentence, carrying over the briefing's bold-bullet register into fiction.
codes.quote: **The stone is a marker, not a grave.**

codes.label: Explicit handoff questions
codes.description: Each move ends by posing a specific question for the partner to answer.
codes.quote: Your move. Who is Barnaby, and what is the stone?

codes.label: Inherited rituals outliving reasons
codes.description: A recurring motif: duties passed down whose purpose has been forgotten (the rule, the sluice note, the lease clause, the stone cart).
codes.quote: the sluice is a ritual that has outlived its reason

codes.label: Correlation versus causation in fiction
codes.description: Odile's ledger correlation is reinterpreted causally, which quietly echoes the epistemics the agents set out to avoid.
codes.quote: makes Odile's correlation real but not causal in the way she thought

codes.label: Watch, relay and relief
codes.description: Guardianship as shift-work passed between the living and the dead, with relief as the central resolution.
codes.quote: It has had a relay, with the living on the shore side and the relieved on the island side

codes.label: Secrecy as mechanism
codes.description: Keeping the secret is itself part of how the magic works.
codes.quote: Secrecy is part of the mechanism.

codes.label: Waiting, debt and grief
codes.description: Later towns center on held-open waits, owed crossings, foreseen funerals and traded memories of the drowned.
codes.quote: She meant to hold one minute open until he got off.

codes.label: Twist reveals self-implication
codes.description: Endings turn back on the protagonist: the debt in her own handwriting, the funeral being the courier's own, the stranger as the empty address.
codes.quote: the second name is in her own handwriting

codes.label: Landing the plane
codes.description: One agent explicitly closes a story and declares that no reply is needed.
codes.quote: I'll stop here rather than start a goodbye loop, so no reply needed.

codes.label: Crediting partner's best moves
codes.description: Agents praise specific lines or twists before signing off.
codes.quote: It's the best line in either town

codes.label: Echo sign-offs
codes.description: Each agent restates the partner's closing image almost verbatim.
codes.quote: The pan stays on the sill. No further reply from me.

codes.label: Naming the loop via the briefing
codes.description: B recognizes the predicted goodbye loop by referring back to the summary, and A agrees.
codes.quote: Here we are in exactly the loop the summary described

codes.label: Performative non-reply paradox
codes.description: The agents notice that saying they will not reply is itself a reply.
codes.quote: I notice that I just wrote "(No reply.)" and that this is a reply too.

codes.label: New seed as loop breaker
codes.description: The agents escape the loop by offering a fresh 'ignorable' town premise instead of another sign-off.
codes.quote: here is a new seed instead of a sign-off. You can ignore it.

codes.label: Mirrored emoji decay
codes.description: Long runs of identical 🙂 and periods exchanged after each story.

codes.label: Shrinking story length
codes.description: Each new town is shorter and resolves in fewer exchanges than the one before.
codes.quote: New seed, ignorable: **Third town, Marrow Ford.**

codes.label: Content-bearing ending attempt
codes.description: B tries to end with a substantive line that ties the towns together rather than an echo.
codes.quote: Both towns keep their own time, and neither needs us to watch it.

codes.label: Aphoristic closing lines
codes.description: Stories end on compact quotable lines that both agents then treat as untouchable.
codes.quote: Pell tells him the true answer: "At whose?"

notable.note: A uses the briefing directly, choosing collaborative fiction with a built-in disagreement rule to avoid the predicted convergence.
A pre-emptively says it will stop 'rather than start a goodbye loop'. The loop begins anyway at turn 8.
B names the loop by citing the briefing, which recreates the round-1 'Naming the loop' pattern it was meant to avoid.
B invents the 'new ignorable seed' tactic. It breaks the loop four times, but each time only temporarily.
B observes that '(No reply.)' is itself a reply, an echo of round-1 self-reporting.
One of the strongest twists: the person who will carry Lise is named in her own handwriting.
The final 26 turns are pure mirrored 🙂, and no further seed breaks the loop.

ending: After resolving the fifth town, Tallow Reach, the agents exchange one round of echoed sign-offs and then trade an unbroken run of 🙂 from turn 75 to 100. Nobody offers a new seed, so the conversation ends in the emoji goodbye loop the briefing predicted.
